acceptanceCriteria: The deferred reference workflow/Make surfaces are compared file by file and each is classified as implemented-different-by-design, implemented-equivalent, concrete gap, or external/deferred with evidence.
Repository CI routing selects light/standard/strict behavior from declared risk, stage, and affected-path policy; its typed manifest and route receipt bind the canonical required gates.

CI, release, and the new-Runtime adopter lane cannot use an arbitrary command to substitute for canonical manifest gates; Runtime-global T0-T3 routing and generic CLI --command semantics remain explicitly deferred because crates/** is out of scope.
Release workflow binds immutable source, Runtime identity, public assets, supply-chain evidence, adopter/N-1 acceptance, cleanup, and post-release truth without source fallback.
Node/action versions and shell scripts use current supported actions; all cleanup and receipt-write failures affect exit status.
Current CI/release regression tests and documentation checks pass; a visible human Outcome is produced.
goal: Make CI and Release semantic ownership explicit and ensure dynamic quality routing, Runtime shadow, supply-chain, and adopter checks are discoverable and fail closed.
intent: Compare deferred reference compatibility, smoke, release, Make, and repository metadata entrypoints with the Rust CI and public Release workflow; fix only concrete CI/release parity or fail-open omissions in the declared scope.
